points.description: Shows that θss = θd is impossible: at steady state (θ̈=θ̇=0) with θ=θd the PD torque Kp(θd−θ) is zero while gravity torque mgℓ sin90° = 2.4525 N·m ≠ 0 (substitution or torque-balance argument that P-term needs an offset to hold the load). Merely saying 'no integral action' with no argument earns no marks here unless it gives the torque-balance idea.
Correct steady-state equation Kp(θd − θss) = mgℓ sin θss (Kd term vanishes since θ̇=0).

Correct steady-state error: e = 0.049 rad ≈ 2.81°, expressed in degrees. Accept any value 2.7°–2.9° (or 0.047–0.050 rad, with conversion to degrees), by linearisation (e ≈ mgℓ/Kp since cos90°=0), numerical iteration or graphical solution; θss ≈ 87.2° accepted. Small-angle sinθ≈θ about zero is invalid and earns nothing here.

levels.says: Correct method giving the right value or setting up the solution properly, but the answer is left in radians without conversion to degrees, or only θss (e.g. 87.2°) is given without stating the error, or the value falls in the band only via a mixed operating point (e.g. cos60° giving 2.70°).

rubric.notes: Full marks need the impossibility argument, the equation Kp(θd−θss)=mgℓ sinθss, and an error of about 2.8° (2.7°–2.9°). Using small-angle sinθ≈θ loses the final 2 marks. Radians-only answers or unstated error get 1 of the final 2.
rubric.answer_key: mgℓ = 1×9.81×0.25 = 2.4525 N·m. Steady state: Kp(θd−θss) = mgℓ sinθss. If θss=θd, LHS=0 but RHS=2.4525 ≠ 0, so impossible. With e=θd−θss, sinθss ≈ sinθd − e cosθd = 1 (cos90°=0), so e ≈ 2.4525/50 = 0.0491 rad ≈ 2.81°. Numerical solution: θss ≈ 87.19°, e ≈ 2.81°.
